claims: With a massless frictionless wheel and rope in a quasistatic lift, two equal tensions support the load: 2T=W. Rope length is anchor_y + free_end_y - 2 wheel_y + pi radius, so free-end travel is twice load travel. Input work T(2h)=Wh.

The free end is pulled upward in this one-moving-wheel arrangement; no extra fixed wheel is shown. Acceleration, stretching, friction and wheel weight are neglected. The second demonstration halves both displacements.
limitations: Numerical checks complement derivations. Idealized assumptions are stated; illustrative objects are not experimental data.
